newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 26.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Ousted national secretary of the Australian Workers Union Steve Harrison claimed yesterday that the organisation faces serious financial difficulties as a result of four years of factional struggles. Harrison made the claims last month in a letter to theIndustrial Registrar, the body responsible for ensuring that unions comply with financial reporting obligations. Page 1.

Australia's second biggest gold company Newcrest Mining Ltd announced yesterday it was dropping expansion plans for its main operation, the Telfer mine in Western Australia, and downgrading the value of the project by A$100 million. Managing director Ian Johnson said the move was necessary to restore Newcrest's credibility with finance institutions and to ensure funding for its planned A$450 million gold exploration project at Cadia in New South Wales. Page 1.

The payments card market in Australia is set for a significant increase in competition as major companies Westfield Property, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Woolworths and Crown Casino all launch their own products on the smartcard market in the near futre. Technological developments will allow the new products to offer consumers greater use of their cards and better rewards. Page 1.

Federal Small Business Minister Geoff Prosser has come under increasing pressure to resign following new claims that he has breached the Prime Minister's ministerial code of conduct by lobbying for his personal business interests while still in office. Aformer Perth councillor has confirmed that Prosser personally contacted him in April this year about a supermarket development. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Federal Small Business Minister Geoff Prosser was last night accused of making personal appeals to former Perth Labor shire councillor John McCourt in an attempt to further his private business interests. The charge by the Federal Opposition is the most serious evidence yet concerning Prosser's alleged breaching of the Prime Minister's code of ministerial conduct. Page 1.

NSW Opposition Leader Peter Collins yesterday called on the Federal Government to allow the constitutional convention on the republic to proceed. Following the Government's refusal to accept a Labor amendment to the convention legislation which would hav assured compulsory voting for delegates, Collins argued that the republic issue should not be used by the Government as a forum to experiment with Australia's voting system. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard has revealed the duties of a politician, particularly Prime Ministers, on overseas trips include attending boring official functions which waste time. Howard, however, evidently enjoyed himself at the opening of The Ashes, a crcket exhibition at Australia House in London which was attended by the Australian cricket team and prominent past players. Page 1.

Research by South Australia's school of information systems leader Terry Robbins-Jones has revealed that managers spend up to 40 per cent of their time in meetings which often have few productive outcomes or promote wrong conclusions. Robbins-Jones beliees that Australian managers are still reluctant to adopt technology used in Europe and the United States which reduces the length of meetings. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

A report by the Centre for Population and Urban Research at Monash University and published in the centre's June bulletin, People and Place, reveals that approximately one third of Australians are dependent on welfare and that 41 per cent of children unde 15 live in low-income families. The report warns there has been an increase of 33 per cent in the number of people claiming welfare in the past 15 years. Page 1.

The Community Service Commission has been asked to investigate claims of serious abuse at a home for the disabled in Sydney's west, the Royal Place at Wentworthville. A report by the Department of Community Services documents a range of abuses committed mong residents and also cases of residents assaulting staff. Page 1.

Federal Small Business Minister Geoff Prosser has been accused of further breaches of the ministerial code of conduct and pressure for his resignation is mounting. Former Perth councillor John McCourt has confirmed Opposition claims that Prosser telephond him in April this year about a shopping centre development. Page 2.

The NSW Government has yielded to a public outcry and announced it will remove three exhaust stacks from residential areas and purchase homes lying above a four-kilometre tunnel connected to the M5 East motorway. However, it has rejected calls for the rod corridor to be moved back to its original position under the Wolli Creek Valley, claiming the extra construction costs could amount to A$171 million. Page 3.
THE AGE

A Monash University report has found that government welfare payments are now a major source of income for one in three adult Australians, and that 41 per cent of children are being raised in households dependent on welfare for economic survival. The reprt forecasts that the financial burden on the Federal Government is set to worsen as the proportion of elderly Australians increases. Page 1.

Former head of the commission appointed to restructure Melbourne's City Council after it was disbanded in 1993, Kevan Gosper, claims the organisation should be abolished and its responsibilities taken over by the State Government. Under Gosper's plan, th role of Lord Mayor would be assumed by the Premier or nominated Minister, who would receive reports from a appointed commission responsible for the city's administration. Page 1.

The Victorian Government has reversed an earlier decision and announced it will not approve the construction of a new chemical storage depot at Point Lillias. The Government has apparently yielded to pressure by conservationists who were concerned the faility would further endanger the rare orange-bellied parrot which has its habitat in the Point Lillias area. Page 1.

Victorian police are continuing efforts to locate missing toddler Jaidyn Leskie, 12 days after his disappearance. Yesterday police concentrated search efforts on the Yallourn rubbish tip at Moe, with the search being resumed there and at Lake Narrocan toay. Page 1.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
